method: Live GitHub Contents/Trees API reads (gh CLI). Executable verification: pip install aspose-cells-foss==26.10.0 into an isolated venv (Python 3.13.15) and ran every documented Quick-start snippet verbatim, plus the Supported-formats table claims, plus the optional skia-python PDF path.

facts.claim: PyPI package matches this source_revision's pyproject.toml version
facts.evidence: pip show aspose-cells-foss -> Version: 26.10.0; pyproject.toml at source_revision -> version = "26.10.0" (implicit via project.version absence resolved from package metadata; Requires: olefile, pycryptodome matches dependencies list).

facts.claim: Core runtime dependencies are pycryptodome>=3.15.0 and olefile>=0.46
facts.evidence: pyproject.toml dependencies = ["pycryptodome>=3.15.0", "olefile>=0.46"]; pip show confirms Requires: olefile, pycryptodome.

facts.claim: Create a workbook, set cell values via A1 refs, workbook.save('report.xlsx') works
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: README's exact 'Create a workbook' snippet run verbatim, produced a non-empty report.xlsx.
Reproduced live: reloaded report.xlsx, worksheet.cells['B2'].value == 1250.50 exactly as set.
Reproduced live: README's 'Apply cell styling' snippet run verbatim, produced non-empty styled.xlsx with no exception.
Reproduced live: README's 'Add a validation list' snippet run verbatim, produced non-empty validation.xlsx.

facts.claim: workbook.save() to .csv/.json/.md infers format from extension and succeeds
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: all three saves from a loaded report.xlsx succeeded, all three output files non-empty.

facts.claim: PDF export requires skia-python, not installed by the core package; fails without it
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: in a venv with only the core package installed, workbook.save('report.pdf') raised RuntimeError: 'PDF export requires skia-python; install the package dependencies' -- not a generic crash, a deliberate guarded message.

facts.claim: Installing skia-python>=144.0.post2,<145 as documented enables PDF export
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: pip install "skia-python>=144.0.post2,<145" into the same venv, then workbook.save('report_with_skia.pdf') succeeded, produced a 17371-byte PDF.

facts.claim: workbook.save(path, password=...) then Workbook(path, password=...) round-trips an encrypted .xlsx
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: README's 'Encrypt a workbook' snippet run verbatim; loaded.worksheets[0].cells['A1'].value == 'Confidential' after password-protected round trip.

facts.claim: CSV import is available through Workbook.load_csv() or load_csv_workbook()
facts.evidence: Reproduced live: both Workbook.load_csv (bound method) and aspose.cells_foss.load_csv_workbook (module-level function) exist; load_csv_workbook('in.csv') on a 2-cell CSV fixture returned a Workbook with a non-None A1 value.

Reproduced live: workbook.save('report.tsv') succeeded (3 bytes for a 1-cell sheet); Workbook('report.tsv') raised BadZipFile (the loader unconditionally treats the input as an OOXML zip container, confirming TSV is write-only as the table states).

facts.claim: Scope section: formats other than .xlsx (.xls, .ods, .xlsb) are not supported
facts.evidence: Not independently executed in this session (no .xls/.ods/.xlsb fixture tried against Workbook()); consistent with the loader module list (only xml_loader.py / csv_handler.py / cfb_handler.py for the encrypted-OOXML case appear in the source tree, no xls/ods/xlsb-specific module), but not proven by direct reproduction. Treat as UNVERIFIED pending a dedicated negative test.

facts.claim: (structural, not factual) This repository's README section skeleton matches the other 6 Cells-family siblings (Navigation, At a Glance mermaid diagram, Key Capabilities, ..., Scope and Limitations with an Enterprise Edition cross-link, ...)
facts.evidence: Direct comparison against the .NET/Cpp/Java/Go/Rust/TypeScript siblings (all read in full this session): every one of the other 6 repositories' READMEs has a Navigation list, an At a Glance mermaid flowchart, and a 'these limitations don't apply to [Enterprise Edition]' cross-link paragraph inside Scope and Limitations. This repository's live README has none of the three -- it uses a flatter heading set (Features, Installation, Quick start, Supported formats, Scope, Examples and API, Development, License) with no Navigation, no At a Glance diagram, and no Enterprise Edition cross-link anywhere. This is a structural, not a factual, finding -- no content claim in the live README is false -- but it is a genuine, checkable divergence from this repository's own family pattern. The Enterprise Edition target URL (https://products.aspose.com/cells/python-net/) used in the Lane R candidate's added cross-link was independently confirmed live (HTTP 200).
